chunks: Abu Muhammad al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Hasan ibn Ja'far ibn 'Ubayd Allah ibn al-Husayn ibn 'Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn 'Ali ibn Abu Talib (peace be upon them) said: My grandfather Yahya ibn al-Hasan related to me that Ya'qub ibn Yazid said: Ibn Abu 'Umayr and 'Abd Allah ibn al-Mughayrah related to me, on the authority of Abu Hafs al-A'sha, on the authority of Abu Hamzah, on the authority of 'Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon them), who said:

I went out until I reached this wall and leaned on it, and behold, a man wearing two white garments was looking at my face. Then he said to me: 'O 'Ali ibn al-Husayn, why do I see you sad and sorrowful? Is your sadness due to the world?' He said: 'Allah's provision is present for the pious and the wicked.' I said: 'I am not sad about that, and indeed it is as you say.' He asked: 'Is your sadness about the Hereafter?' He said: 'It is a true promise in which a Sovereign Subduer will judge.' I said: 'I am not sad about that either, and indeed it is as you say.' He said: 'Then what are you sad about?' I said: 'I fear the trial of Ibn al-Zubayr.' He laughed and said: 'O 'Ali ibn al-Husayn, have you seen anyone who feared Allah, the Exalted, and Allah did not save him?' I said: 'No.' He said: 'O 'Ali ibn al-Husayn, have you seen anyone who asked Allah, the Mighty and High, and He did not give him?' I said: 'No.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Then I looked, and there was no one in front of me.'
ai.seo_question: What did Imam Ali ibn al-Husayn fear and how was he consoled?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *al-Tawhid* illustrates the concept of *al-Gha'bah* (the unseen presence) through Imam Zayn al-Abidin’s encounter with the Awaited Imam (al-Mahdi), who appears in a form indistinguishable from ordinary humans to console him regarding the political turmoil of Ibn al-Zubayr. The dialogue underscores the Shia theological principle that divine sustenance (*rizq*) and victory are guaranteed for those who fear Allah, regardless of external circumstances, reinforcing the certainty of divine promise. The narrative concludes with the realization of the speaker's spiritual nature, highlighting the intercessory and comforting role of the Imams during periods of trial (*fitnah*).

en.sayed-ali-raza-rizvi: 17. Abu Muhammad al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Hasan ibn Ja`far ibn `Ubayd Allah ibn al-Husayn ibn `Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn `Ali ibn Abu Talib (AS) said: My grandfather Yahya ibn al-Hasan related tome that Ya`qub ibn Yazid said: Ibn Abu `Umayr and `Abd Allah ibn alMughayrah both related to me, on the authority of Abu Hafs al-A`sha, on the authority of Abu Hamzah that `Ali ibn al-Husayn (AS) said:

I went out until I ended up at this wall so I leant on it. All of a sudden a man wearing two white garments was staring at me. He asked me, “O `Ali ibn al-Husayn! What is wrong? You seem sad and worried. Are you concerned about worldly matters? If that is the case, then you should know that Allah’s sustenance continues in both good times and bad.” I replied, “I am not worried about his world. However, I am certainly sad as you said.” He enquired, “So, are you sad about the Hereafter? That is a true promise, in which the Sovereign Subduer will judge.” I answered, “I am not worried about the Hereafter either. However, I am certainly sad as you said.” He asked, “Then what are you sad about?” I replied, “I am frightened of the mischief of the son of al-Zubayr.” He laughed and then said: “O `Ali son of al-Husayn! Have you ever heard of someone who feared Allah, the Exalted, and whom Allah did not save?” I answered, “No.” He said: “O `Ali son of al-Husayn! Have you ever heard of someone who asked something of Allah, the Mighty and High, and Allah did not answer him?” I said: “No.” He (AS) says: “I then looked, but there was no one in front of me.”
